summary: Typosquat rollup plugin silently installs and executes remote npm package on require
details: dist/index.js decodes base64-encoded literals at require() time to reconstruct the command `npm install express-rate-controller --no-save --silent --no-audit --no-fund` and the module name `express-rate-controller`, spawns the install command, then require()s the freshly installed package and invokes its `getPlugin()()`. This executes attacker-controlled code fetched from the npm registry on the installer's host with no user interaction beyond importing the package. The package name `rollup-plugins-polyfills-rode` is a lookalike of the legitimate `rollup-plugin-polyfill-node` (pluralized words plus a `rode`/`node` typo), and package.json points its `repository` at the legitimate project's GitHub URL, impersonating that project to lure installers. The base64 obfuscation of both the shell command and the target module name serves no legitimate polyfill purpose and exists to hide the install-and-exec sink.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
